June · Listen & Shadow · Three Conversations V

The Friday Report — reporting back, rebuilding trust
D O   E N G L I S H   W I T H   B R I A N
TALK 1 · WHAT YOU STUMBLED INTO
👤 Friend
What good things did you stumble into — not plan?
계획 없이 굴러들어온 좋은 일, 뭐가 있었어?
stumble into ~ — 우연히 ~하게 되다
💬 June
I stumbled into Pilates by pure chance.
필라테스는 순전히 우연으로 시작했어.
by pure chance — 순전히 우연으로
같은 패턴으로 — I stumbled into research by pure chance. · He stumbled into teaching after one favor.
💬 June
I happened to enroll in a class on a whim.
어쩌다 보니 어느 수업에 등록하게 됐거든.
on a whim — 즉흥적으로 · enroll — 등록하다
같은 패턴으로 — I happened to sit next to her that day. · We happened to take the same elevator.
💬 June
It wasn't part of the plan.
그건 계획에 없던 일이었어.
part of ~ — ~의 일부
같은 패턴으로 — Grad school wasn't part of the plan. · Seoul wasn't part of the plan either.
💬 June
One thing led to another.
하나가 다음으로 이어지더라.
lead to ~ — ~로 이어지다
💬 June
At the time it felt like nothing — looking back, it was a turning point.
그때는 별일 아니었는데, 돌아보면 전환점이었어.
turning point — 전환점
같은 패턴으로 — At the time it felt small — looking back, it changed everything. · Looking back, that call was the start.
💬 June
If I hadn't taken that class, I'd never have ended up here.
그 수업을 안 들었다면, 이 길로 못 왔을 거야.
end up — 결국 ~하게 되다
같은 패턴으로 — If I hadn't missed the bus, I'd never have met him. · If she hadn't asked, I'd never have applied.
TALK 2 · WAITING VS. CHASING
👤 Friend
Can you invite luck — or only wait for it?
운은 부를 수 있는 걸까, 기다릴 수밖에 없는 걸까?
invite — 부르다, 초대하다
💬 June
You can't force it.
억지로 되게 할 수는 없다고 봐.
force — 억지로 하게 하다
같은 패턴으로 — You can't force a friendship. · You can't force good timing.
💬 June
But you can put yourself in the way of it.
하지만 그 일이 일어날 길목에 나를 둘 수는 있지.
in the way of ~ — ~의 길목에
같은 패턴으로 — I put myself in the way of new people. · She puts herself in the way of chances.
💬 June
I'm the type to show up anyway — even when I don't feel like it.
나는 일단 나가는 쪽이야 — 기분이 안 따라줘도.
show up — 나타나다, 참석하다
같은 패턴으로 — He's the type to show up anyway. · Show up anyway — that's half of it.
💬 June
Some things I didn't find — they found me.
어떤 건 내가 찾아낸 게 아니라, 그게 나를 찾아왔어.
find — 찾다
같은 패턴으로 — The job found me. · That idea found me in the shower.
💬 June
The harder I chase something, the faster it runs.
너무 세게 쫓으면, 오히려 도망가.
chase — 쫓다
같은 패턴으로 — The harder I push, the worse it gets. · The more I plan, the less it happens.
TALK 3 · WHEN CHANCE BECOMES FATE
👤 Friend
Why does randomness look like destiny once it's behind us?
우연은 왜 지나고 나면 운명처럼 보일까?
randomness — 무작위성 · destiny — 운명
💬 June
In hindsight, the dots connect.
지나고 보면, 점들이 이어져.
in hindsight — 지나고 보면 · connect the dots — 점을 잇다
같은 패턴으로 — In hindsight, it all fell into place. · In hindsight, the timing was perfect.
💬 June
In the midst of it, it wasn't a story — it was just noise.
그 한가운데선 이야기가 아니라 그냥 소음이었어.
in the midst of ~ — ~의 한가운데서 · noise — 소음
같은 패턴으로 — In the midst of it, it just felt like work. · In the middle of it, nothing made sense.
💬 June
When things line up too perfectly, I do get suspicious.
너무 완벽하게 맞아떨어지면, 의심이 들긴 해.
line up — 맞아떨어지다 · suspicious — 의심스러운
같은 패턴으로 — When a deal looks too perfect, I get careful. · When it's too easy, I double-check.
💬 June
Do we find the meaning — or make it up afterward?
의미를 발견하는 걸까, 나중에 만들어내는 걸까?
afterward — 나중에, 그 후에
같은 패턴으로 — Do we choose the path — or explain it afterward?
💬 June
It only makes sense backwards.
인생은 뒤로만 말이 되는 것 같아.
backwards — 거꾸로, 뒤로
같은 패턴으로 — The season only makes sense backwards. · Careers only make sense backwards.
💬 June
In the end, we turn chance into a story.
결국 우리는 우연을 이야기로 바꾸는 거지.
in the end — 결국 · chance — 우연
같은 패턴으로 — We turn pain into a story. · She turned that accident into her best chapter.
느리게 20/20 · 보통 20/20
